heading: EXT. THE LANTERN MARKET - MOONLIT BRIDGE - NIGHT

units.text: EXT. THE LANTERN MARKET - MOONLIT BRIDGE - NIGHT
Paper lanterns drift on strings between crooked rooftops, each glowing a different colour.
Stalls cling to a hump-backed stone bridge: spice sellers, mask-carvers, a woman peddling jars of captured starlight.
The river below runs silver.
THESSALY GREYMANTLE, 30s, a cloaked traveller with a staff and a battered satchel, walks the bridge with measured steps, savouring the stillness.
A hush has fallen over the whole market.
Even the birds seem to be listening.
MORVAN, 60s, a stooped old lamplighter with a long pole and a crooked grin, tends a lantern on the parapet.
PIP, 10, a barefoot child in an oversized waistcoat, darts out from behind a stall and plants herself directly in Thessaly's path.
You're new.
units.name: PIP

units.text: I'm passing through.
units.name: THESSALY

units.text: Everyone says that.
units.name: PIP

units.text: What a lovely evening.
units.name: THESSALY

units.text: No answer.
The stall-keepers do not look up.
Morvan hangs his pole against the wall, wipes his hands, and slides a step closer to Pip.
Pip. Come away from the lady.
units.name: MORVAN

units.text: She's nice.
units.name: PIP

units.text: She's not nice. She's early.
units.name: MORVAN

units.text: Thessaly's smile does not change, but her hand slips to the head of her staff.

The lanterns overhead flicker, one by one, from warm gold to a cold, flat white, and the crowd on the bridge, slowly, wordlessly, turns to face her, while Morvan lifts Pip off her feet and sets her behind him, Pip squirming, Thessaly tilting her head, and the child at last whispering something to the lamplighter that makes his crooked grin vanish completely.
She's the one from the story.
units.name: PIP

units.text: Of course I am.
units.name: THESSALY

units.text: She raises the staff.
The river stops moving.
